text:
Your deck buries its best news. The 40% month-over-month revenue growth doesn't appear until slide nine, after three slides of market-sizing boilerplate.

This matters because investors skimming a seed pitch decide within the first 3 minutes. DocSend's averages put the whole deck at often under 4 minutes. Your traction metric is the one number your fundraising argument depends on, and it arrives after attention has already left the room. Investors may also assume the hiding was deliberate.

Your opening slide currently headlines a mission statement. The data should sit at the front instead.

**Suggested fixes:**
- Make slide two lead with growth, then the customer acquisition cost payback period of 5 months, then the problem.
- Cut the TAM preamble to one line.
- Let traction do the talking.

As it stands, the deck reads like a slow-reveal mystery novel, where the reader skips to the last chapter or quits.
